_status: Module 4, Try it 4.2A 'Safe or suspicious?' and its model answers (learner guide of 21 October 2026, pages 7, 16 and 17): six screens, the clue, and what to do. Fictional office; .example names are reserved for documentation.

browser.title: [[c1|Your connection is not private]]
browser.via: Dan opens the office's leave portal, as every month

messages.body: Attackers might be trying to steal your information from leave.rsso-q.example (for example, passwords, messages or credit cards). [[c2|NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID]]

cues.text: A full-page warning means the browser **could not confirm the site's identity**.
The usual cause on an office system is an expired or wrongly set-up certificate, which IT must fix.

messages.why: Do not click past it or sign in; tell IT, who will usually find an expired or wrongly set-up certificate. Staff should never learn to ignore the warning.

browser.title: RSSO Assistance Portal: payout problem
browser.via: [[c2|Opened from a link in a text message about a payout problem]]
browser.button: Sign in to fix your payout

messages.body: Your payout is on hold. Sign in within 24 hours to keep your assistance.

cues.text: **A zero in place of the letter o:** the owner is rss0-q.example, not rsso-q.example.
It arrived by SMS link, with a deadline. **The padlock proves nothing:** it means private, not honest.

messages.why: Do not sign in; report the text. If you already entered a password, change it at once from the real address and tell IT.

browser.title: Merge PDFs free! No sign-up
browser.via: A colleague, needing to merge two beneficiary masterlists before noon

messages.body: Drop your files here. [[c2|We may keep uploaded files to improve our service.]]

cues.text: **Sensitive personal data** going to an outside service.
**No agreement** with the RSSO: the office cannot control, see or recall the files.

messages.why: Stop; use an approved tool or ask IT. The office stays responsible for that data (RA 10173, Secs 14 and 21(a)).

messages.body: [[c2|Download the update now]] to keep browsing safely.

cues.text: **Updates do not arrive through pop-ups on other websites.**
An unexpected download: do not open it.

messages.why: Close the tab; update through the browser itself or ask IT. If a pop-up says your computer is infected and gives a number to call, never call it: close the browser and tell IT.

browser.title: RSSO Assistance Portal · Staff sign-in
browser.via: [[c2|Ben opens it from his own bookmark]]

messages.body: Welcome back, Ben. Sign in with your security key.

cues.text: The owner part is **rsso-q.example**: the real address.
Typed from his own bookmark, not a link in a message.

messages.why: Carry on. Bookmarks and typed addresses you know are the safest habit; a password manager also helps, because it offers your password only on the address where you saved it.

messages.verdict: Suspicious: IDs in a chat group

cues.text: **An unapproved messaging group:** outside the office's control and records.
**ID images of applicants** and health information.

messages.why: Stop posting; move checks into the portal or an approved tool; tell the DPO, who decides whether this is a breach.
